name: Buz
overview: Buz was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known primarily as the father of Jahdo. He is identified as a Gadite, linking him to the descendants of Gad, one of the twelve sons of Jacob. Beyond his role as Jahdo's father, Scripture does not provide additional details about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Buz means 'contempt' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name rather than a title. This meaning is noted in 1 Chronicles 5:15, though the name was not given by God. The significance of the name is not elaborated upon in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Buz is recorded as the father of Jahdo, establishing a direct paternal relationship. He is also a descendant of Gad, connecting him to the tribal lineage of Gad. Scripture does not mention other family relationships beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Buz's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position within the genealogy of the Gadites, emphasizing the continuity of the tribe through his lineage. As the father of Jahdo, he contributes to the ancestral record that highlights the preservation of God's covenant people. His mention, though brief, supports the broader biblical theme of God's faithfulness in maintaining tribal identities among Israel.
